faq.sectionSubtitle: Everything you need to know about in-browser video reframing
faq.q1: How do I change a video from landscape to portrait without cropping out important parts?
faq.a1: Select the 9:16 vertical preset and choose 'Blur'. This scales your original horizontal video to fit cleanly within the vertical canvas while automatically filling the top and bottom with a soft, blurred duplicate of the video.
faq.q2: What aspect ratio is best for YouTube Shorts, TikTok, and Instagram Reels?
faq.a2: All three vertical short-form platforms require a 9:16 aspect ratio (recommended resolution: 1080 x 1920 pixels). Ensuring key titles are kept inside the central safe zone avoids overlap with UI buttons.
faq.q3: Does changing aspect ratio reduce video quality?
faq.a3: Not with AspectCut. Video frames are re-encoded directly on your device CPU using WebCodecs. When audio codecs match the container (such as AAC in MP4), the audio stream is copied bit-for-bit without generational loss.
faq.q4: Are my private videos uploaded to your servers?
faq.a4: Never. Your video file is read into your browser's local sandbox memory and transformed using client-side WebCodecs. No bytes are sent across the network, ensuring complete privacy.
faq.q5: What video formats and maximum file sizes are supported?
faq.a5: AspectCut accepts MP4, MOV, WebM, and MKV containers up to 500 MB in size.
faq.q6: Why do exported videos need even-numbered pixel dimensions?
faq.a6: Modern video codecs like H.264 and HEVC utilize YUV 4:2:0 chroma subsampling, requiring pixel widths and heights to be divisible by 2. Odd pixel dimensions cause hardware decoding crashes or green line artifacts.
faq.q7: How does the ambient blurred background extension work?
faq.a7: AspectCut places your original footage centered at full resolution in the middle, while generating an enlarged, heavily blurred duplicate layer behind it to elegantly fill empty letterbox bars.
faq.q8: Can I convert video aspect ratios on mobile devices like iPhone or Android?
faq.a8: Yes. AspectCut executes directly in modern mobile browsers (iOS Safari 16+ and Android Chrome) with WebCodecs support, letting you export directly to your device camera roll without installing native apps.
